explanation: The last days before the end of the world, which Jesus describes as being marked by great events, war, and persecution.
Pretenders who claim to be the Messiah but lead people away from the truth.
Conflicts between nations that are a sign that the end is near.
Lack of food and famine that will strike many places in the world.
Natural disasters such as shaking of the earth, often seen as part of the great tribulations.
Unfair treatment and threats against believers because they hold fast to their faith in Jesus.
The period when non-Jewish peoples have the opportunity to hear the gospel before the end comes.
Visible phenomena in the sky such as the sun becoming dark and the moon not shining, signaling God's judgment.
A title Jesus uses for himself to describe his role as the coming judge with full authority.
Holy beings who will gather the chosen from all ends of the earth when the time comes.
The moment when the bride (the church) is united with the Bridegroom (Jesus), often compared to a sudden event.
Being awake and aware that one does not know the day or hour of God's coming, which requires spiritual readiness.
